newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slide on U.S. market slump.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slide on U.S. market slump.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished much lower Friday as a downturn sparked by falling U.S. markets built up losses late in the session.
The negative impact started with U.S. Treasuries but even as they stabilized through the session, sharp falls of more than three percent in U.S. stocks kept the downward momentum in Argentine bonds.
"I do not see any symptoms of panic," said an analyst at an Argentine brokerage house.
Argentina's Par Brady bond fell 7/8 to 73-1/2 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 fell $0.10 to 119.90.
However, the market has been rocked with volatility this week. "The market is volatile but that is all because of volatility in U.S. markets," said a trader.
"Here there are no alarming singals," he added.
With the outlook completely dependent on the movements of U.S. markets next week, traders were loath to make any predictions for the Argentine market.
Argentine markets are closed Monday for a bank holiday.
In the money market, one-week peso BAIBOR, or the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, was flat at 7.1875 percent.
